pr_title: Bluetooth: Host: Cap EATT MTU so it's symmetric
pr_body:
The Specification mandates this. The same logic is already implemented for UATT.

Fixes: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/53475

Signed-off-by: Aleksander Wasaznik <aleksander.wasaznik@nordicsemi.no>

issue_context.title: The ATT_MTU value for EATT should be set as the minimum MTU of ATT Client and ATT Server
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
BLUETOOTH CORE SPECIFICATION Version 5.3 | Vol 3, Part G page 1528
[GATT] 5.3 ENHANCED ATT BEARER L2CAP INTEROPERABILITY REQUIREMENTS
5.3.1 ATT_MTU
**The ATT_MTU for the Enhanced ATT bearer shall be set to the minimum of the
MTU field values of the two devices**; these values come from the L2CAP_CREDIT_BASED_CONNECTION_REQ and L2CAP_CREDIT_BASED_CONNECTION_RSP signaling packets or the latest L2CAP_CREDIT_BASED_RECONFIGURE_REQ packets.
Note: The minimum ATT_MTU for an Enhanced ATT bearer is 64 octets.

From the specification, we can see that ATT_MTU for EATT should be chosen as the  the minimum of the MTU of ATT client and ATT server. This has the same behavior as ATT.

**To Reproduce**
The current implementation in zephyr does not follow the "ENHANCED ATT BEARER L2CAP INTEROPERABILITY REQUIREMENTS". When EATT is connected, TX MTU and RX MTU can be different. GATT send ATT PDU size as TX MTU (bt_att_get_mtu) without considering RX MTU. In other words, maximum ATT PDU size can be different for different direction.

**Expected behavior**
Follow the "ENHANCED ATT BEARER L2CAP INTEROPERABILITY REQUIREMENTS", set ATT_MTU for EATT as the  the minimum of the MTU of ATT client and ATT server, so that maximum ATT PDU size is the same for different direction.

**Impact**
Different maximum ATT PDU size for sending and receiving will cause a lot of issues.
Issue 1:
When handling GATT read response, TX MTU is used to check whether it is a long characteristic, but real received payload size is decided by RX MTU.
Issue 2:
When sending "Prepare Write", TX MTU is used to set payload size, the same payload shall be returned by ATT server with the same EATT bearer, but RX MTU might be smaller than TX MTU, ATT client has no way to check the response successfully.

Hope that I didn't miss something in the specification.
Please help to check.

review_comments: Should this function be used all the places where we do `tx.mtu = mtu`?

Yes, when outside of `l2cap.c` at least. But I wanted to keep this PR minimal. I can post a follow up later.

I'll take this chance to explain why it's nice to define a function like this, even though the body is obvious: It makes it clear that this "hack" is OK by the L2CAP layer. I think `chan.tx.mtu` was originally intended to be what I name `chan.remote.rx.mtu`. In that case, directly setting `chan.tx.mtu` looks like writing to a "read-only" value. We are making it clear that `chan.tx.mtu` is something different than `chan.remote.rx.mtu`.
The MPS is no longer being set, is that intentional?

Yes. The intention of the surrounding code is to set up enforcing of the ATT_MTU for outgoing messages. And the MPS is not relevant to this. There is some smart programming here, which we'll see saves us some bytes at the cost of clarity: 

The simple / self-contained way of doing this would be to define a new field `bt_att_chan.att_mtu` [^1], and enforce it inside the ATT layer.

But the smart hack is that we can store the att_chan.ATT_MTU in `le_chan->tx.mtu`. This saves us two bytes of RAM per EATT bearer. It also has the nice side-effect making the L2CAP layer refuse to send the message with a `-EMSGSIZE` if the message is larger than the ATT_MTU, even if it would fit in the L2CAP MTU. This allows us to offload the MTU checking to the L2CAP layer, saving us some bytes of ROM.

As you can see, the MPS plays no role here. The ATT_MTU check is enforced by the L2CAP MTU setting. It is not OK to override the L2CAP MTU/MPS to larger than it truly is, so increasing it is not possible. And on the other hand if the MPS is larger than it needs to be, it does not matter.

[^1]: This can also be a function, since the ATT_MTU is at all times equal to `min(remote.rx.mtu, local.tx.mtu, local.rx.mtu)`, where `remote.rx.mtu=le_chan.tx.mtu`, `local.tx.mtu=CONFIG_BT_L2CAP_TX_MTU`, `local.rx.mtu=le_chan.rx.mtu`. `remote.rx.mtu` and `local.tx.mtu` are true limits on what fits in the buffers. The limit `local.rx.mtu` is arbitrary, but it is mandated by the spec.
